1.text: Buckingham Palace has its own post office, cinema, swimming pool and doctor's surgery. Its garden is the largest private garden in London.

2.text: From the top of the Burj Khalifa the sun stays in view for several minutes after it has set at ground level. Residents high up the tower wait a few extra minutes to break their Ramadan fast.

3.text: People have lived aboard the International Space Station without a break since 2 November 2000. It is the longest continuous human presence in space.

4.text: Venus spins the opposite way to most planets, including Earth. If you could see through its clouds, the Sun would rise in the west and set in the east.

5.text: Lake Baikal is the world's oldest lake, at 25 to 30 million years, and holds nearly a fifth of the planet's unfrozen fresh water. Its seal, the nerpa, lives nowhere else.

6.text: The US Navy wanted the Golden Gate Bridge painted in black and yellow stripes so ships could see it. Architect Irving Morrow chose International Orange, which suits the surroundings and shows up in fog.

7.text: The Moon is drifting away from Earth by about 3.8 cm a year. Scientists measure it by bouncing laser beams off mirrors that Apollo astronauts left on the surface.

8.text: The International Space Station was built in orbit, mostly from parts carried up by the Space Shuttle and fitted by astronauts using robotic arms and spacewalks. Five space agencies from fifteen countries are involved.

9.text: Five foghorns were set up on the Golden Gate Bridge in 1937 and still work today. They are air-powered and switched on and off by hand.

10.text: The Sydney Opera House's roof tiles were made in Sweden by Höganäs, in two colours: glossy white and matt cream. Its Danish architect, Jørn Utzon, left Australia before it opened and never returned.
